AccessState.description: What the sign-in needs to know (the web app's AccessInfo).
AccessState.title: AccessState

Choice.description: One entry of a drop-down: what it shows and what it stores.
Choice.title: Choice

DataCredit.description: Whose data a provider or data source downloads, from its descriptor's `credit`.
DataCredit.title: DataCredit

Descriptor.description: An installed plugin, data source or display's descriptor (its `*-info.json`): open, its keys are the descriptor's (the web app reads them as `FormDefs.ts`'s `Descriptor`).
Descriptor.title: Descriptor

Document.description: A settings document: its `_id` and `_rev`, and keys only its schema or descriptor knows. Open: every key is passed on, none is checked here.
Document.title: Document

Done.description: The answer of a change that worked and has nothing else to say.
Done.title: Done

InkColor.description: One ink of the panel: its name, the exact color the app draws with and hands to the driver, and roughly the color the panel shows.
InkColor.title: InkColor

InvalidTask.description: A task whose trigger cannot be evaluated, and why in our words.
InvalidTask.title: InvalidTask

Load.description: Each reading only when the machine gives it.
Load.title: Load

Located.description: A rough position, or our words for why there is none.
Located.title: Located

Owner.description: A plugin's or a data source's folder: `kept_bytes` are its kept downloads and answers.
Owner.title: Owner

PanelInks.description: The inks of the panel, in palette order. `confirmed` is false while the display has not started: the set is then a guess from the display settings.
PanelInks.title: PanelInks

Period.description: A data source's calls in a period: by status (or why there was none), the bytes, and what its cache did.
Period.title: Period

Pi.description: A Raspberry Pi's own readings: the model always, the others when the Pi gives them.
Pi.title: Pi

ProviderChoice.description: A provider of a capability: `ready` when its own settings are complete (its name says so too).
ProviderChoice.title: ProviderChoice

Pushed.description: A pushed message or picture: the `id` that takes it down, the title it is known by (made unique), and the least it waits.
Pushed.title: Pushed

Rendered.description: The runs of the timer tasks over the days asked for, in the device zone (`timezone`), with the documents they belong to.
Rendered.title: Rendered

RestoreSummary.description: What a restore would do (or did), by name: never a value.
RestoreSummary.title: RestoreSummary

Role.description: A role of the palette: its CSS class and its color as `hsl()`.
Role.title: Role

RowStep.description:
A row action's answer, always 200: what to show next (`message`, a `link` to open, a `code` to enter, an `input` to fill, or a wait of `poll` seconds) and the run's `session`,
until it is `done` with `ok` and its last `message`. Each field only when the step has it.
RowStep.title: RowStep

Run.description: A time a task runs, with its offset.
Run.title: Run

Saved.description: A document that was stored: its id and its new revision.
Saved.title: Saved

SignedIn.description: Signed in, or nothing to sign in to (`required` false).
SignedIn.title: SignedIn

SoftwareCredit.description: A font or other software by others: whose it is, its licence, and what it does here.
SoftwareCredit.title: SoftwareCredit

Status.description: Whether every part came up, and each part's state in our words.
Status.title: Status

Task.description: What a timer task runs: a plugin and its settings.
Task.title: Task

TestAnswer.description: A Test button's answer, always 200 and in our words: whether it worked, and what to show beside the field.
TestAnswer.title: TestAnswer

TimerItem.description: A timer task on its own, with its document's id and revision (a change to the task changes the document's).
TimerItem.title: TimerItem

TransportState.description: Whether playback is stopped, and where the playlist layer is: its playlist and track by id (left out before its first track).
TransportState.title: TransportState

Upgraded.description: A document from an older version: the versions it is brought from and to.
Upgraded.title: Upgraded

post.description:
Open a backup (`{ "archive": <base64>, "passphrase": ..., "apply": false|true }`). Without `apply` it only says what would change, by name (the summary the person confirms); with it the files
are written. Every document is checked by the rules of the route that would have saved it; with any problem nothing is written. The device password is never touched (a backup does not hold it), and
nothing is deleted: a file in the storage that the backup does not have stays.

schema.description: The backup file (base64), its passphrase, and whether to write it (without, only what would change).
schema.title: RestoreBody

get.description:
The timer task triggers for each of `days` days, starting on the day of `start` (today by default).
Disabled items are not rendered (the timer layer does not run them); items whose trigger is malformed are skipped and listed in `invalid`.

parameters.description: The first day: YYYY-MM-DD (that calendar day), or a time with an offset or Z (its day in the system time zone). A time without an offset is a 422.
parameters.name: start

schema.description: The first day: YYYY-MM-DD (that calendar day), or a time with an offset or Z (its day in the system time zone). A time without an offset is a 422.
schema.title: Start

post.description: Run a stored task now (the Scheduler's Run now): any enabled task that is valid, whatever its trigger. The timer layer runs it on its own; the answer is that it was asked to.

Present the API token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or the device password as `{ "password": "..." }`. When it is right, the server
starts a session and sets the session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, so scripts cannot read it and other sites cannot send it).

schema.description: The device password; the API token is a Bearer header instead, with no body.
schema.title: SignInBody

get.description:
The factory values of a device-wide document, from the copy shipped in the NVE (not the stored schema's, and not the stored document): what a "restore the
default" button puts back in the form (the user saves it, or not). Only values, never the stored document's `_id` or `_rev`.
Whether the display and the two layers came up: `{ ok, components: { name: { state: ok|failed|starting, message } } }`. Our words only.

Numbers and our own words only: no host name, address, user or path. `pi` is present only on a Raspberry Pi. A reading the machine cannot give is left out.
The storage's folders are walked on every call (a few dozen small files); the page asks every ten seconds while it is open.

post.description: A rough position from the device's public IP address, for the Location field's button: `{ ok, message, latitude?, longitude? }`. Nothing is saved; always 200, in our words.

get.description: The kept events newer than `since`, oldest first (a first paint, a script, or catching up).

post.description:
The roles of the palette for these theme settings (what the form holds, saved or not): `[{ name, color }]`, name as the CSS class, color as `hsl()`.
Values that are not valid read as the factory defaults, as they do on the device.

get.description: Whether playback is stopped, for the play/stop button, and the playlist and track the layer is on, for the System page's playlist panel.

post.description:
Forward a command: `play` (resume where it stopped), `stop`, or `next` (the next track; a stopped layer plays from there).
It is accepted, not done: the layer does it on its own thread, and its telemetry says what happened.
